info.title: Evictions API
info.description: Submit and track an eviction case for a rental property in any US state or DC. Evictions API is not a law firm and does not give legal advice. After a live case is submitted we engage a licensed attorney in the property's state for it; nothing is served on a tenant or filed in court until that attorney has reviewed the case, and the attorney serves and files through their own accounts while the case shows its status, documents, deadlines, messages and charges. Test keys are a free developer feature for building and testing an integration: a test key works only with a fictional test state (ZZ), and nothing real is served or filed. A built-in test reviewer approves test cases automatically once they enter review, and `POST /v1/cases/{id}/advance` moves a test case on one step at a time. A request in live mode on a server where live mode is off answers 403 `live_unavailable`. POST requests accept an `Idempotency-Key` header.

get.summary: Whether a jurisdiction is served, and its notice rules

200.description: Served status, `handling`, jurisdiction ids and the grounds. With a live key every US state and DC is served, with the `handling` a case created there gets (`"agent_filed"` where `fullService` is true, `"attorney_direct"` elsewhere), `action: null` and, for each ground, `notice: null` and the facts intake requires (`requiredFacts`) and, where `fullService` is true, the facts that place's documents ask for beyond them (`documentFacts`: `notice` and `filing`, by where the case starts, and `conditional`, facts asked for only when another holds (with `past: true`, when that fact is a date before today, such as a lease end date that has passed), `ledgerItemised`, where the place's documents itemise the ledger by kind of charge (`notice`: the notice demands only what is past due on its date; `filing`: the filing states the amounts by kind), and `defaults`, the pack's own default where a fact has one). They apply to a full-service case: ask an attorney-path case for the intake facts alone; anything else is `served: false`. With a test key (`handling: "automated"`) the fictional test state answers with its notice rules for each ground. `fullService` says whether a case created here with `service: "full"` is handled by us as your agent (no attorney reviews it); where it is false, a managed-service request answers 409 `service_unavailable` with its operational reason. This does not establish a legal requirement for counsel. `county` may be written as the US Census Bureau lists it or by its short name, in any case ("Henry County", "henry"); a county the state does not have answers 400 `invalid_request`. `court` is the court the place's rules say a case goes to, with the county ("Magistrate court of Henry County"), or `null` where no rule pack covers the place. `courts` lists, where `fullService` is true, the courts a full-service case's `managedContext.courtId` may name, each with the `forums` its `managedContext.forum` may name; it is empty otherwise.

post.summary: Read a lease (PDF, JPEG or PNG, at most 4 MB and, for a PDF, 40 pages, as base64) with an AI service (Claude Haiku 4.5 through OpenRouter) and answer the facts the new-case form takes. For a file the free reading on the device could not read. With `kind: "correspondence"` and `files` (1 to 10 messages with the tenant: PDF, JPEG, PNG, plain text `text/plain`, or a saved email `message/rfc822` (`.eml`, at most 1 MB, turned into its text before it is sent); 8 MB, 40 PDF pages and 200,000 characters of text in all), it drafts what happened for a lease-violation case (`violationDescription`, `violationDate`): a draft for the person to read and correct, never a checked answer. One request counts once against the hourly limit, whatever the number of files. With `kind: "ledger"` and one `file` (a tenant ledger PDF, at most 4 MB and 40 pages), it answers the ledger's rows (`rows`, each `{ date, type: "charge" | "payment", amountCents, memo }`, at most 500, in the order printed) a balance brought forward from before them (`openingBalanceCents`, null when none) and the ending balance the ledger states (`endingBalanceCents`, null when it states none), for the caller to check: the balance brought forward and the rows should add up to the ending balance, and the website fills in nothing when they do not. A row dated after today is left out. The files are sent to OpenRouter only for this one reading, under fixed names (the `name` you send is never passed on), on endpoints that keep no data; nothing is stored and nothing of the files or the answer is logged. Every answer is a suggestion for a person to check: a fact the reading is unsure of is left out, never guessed. When the service refuses, fails or takes over 30 seconds, the answer is empty (`{ "suggestions": {}, "confidence": {} }`, or for a ledger `{ "rows": [], "openingBalanceCents": null, "endingBalanceCents": null }`), never an error. For now only the signed-in app and test keys can use it: a live API key answers 503 `extract_unavailable`. At most 20 an hour per organization (429 `rate_limited`); 503 `extract_unavailable` when the server has no AI service set

200.description: The answers found, in the same shape as the website's lease reading: each a `{ value, source: "lease_file" }` (`source: "messages"` for the messages' draft), and how sure the reading is of each (`high` or `medium`). Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`, `monthlyRent` is dollars with cents ("1450.00"), `noticePeriod` is whole days ("3"), `state` is the two-letter code; `parties` lists the landlord (`plaintiff`) and the tenants (`defendant`). From messages: `violationDescription` (a few plain sentences, at most 2,000 characters) and `violationDate` (never later than today).

amountCents.description: Whole cents, always positive; `type` says which way it moves the balance.

openingBalanceCents.description: A balance brought forward from before the first row, in whole cents (negative for a credit); null when the ledger shows none. It is not among `rows`.

endingBalanceCents.description: The balance the ledger states at its end, in whole cents (negative for a credit); null when it states none. `openingBalanceCents` plus the rows should come to it.

post.summary: Create a draft case. For a live case the property must be in a US state or DC (422 `unsupported_state`) and the case takes the full-service path (we act as your agent, no attorney reviews the case) wherever that path is open for the property; elsewhere it is an attorney-direct case. The case's `handling` says which. `service` is not needed for a live case: `"attorney"` selects nothing, and `"full"` where the path is not open answers 409 `service_unavailable` without creating a different service. A test case takes the full-service path only with `service: "full"`

county.description: The county, as the US Census Bureau lists it or by its short name, in any case ("Henry County", "Henry", "henry"). It is stored by its short name ("Henry"); a county the state does not have is refused (400 `invalid_request`).

noticeMethods.description: The additional ways the rental agreement says a notice must be delivered, exactly as the lease states them, or the word `none`. Asked for where a place's notice states them (Georgia): the notice is posted on the door and says it is also delivered by these methods, or that the rental agreement provides none.

kind.description: What a charge is for: `rent`, `late_fee`, `utilities`, `other_fee` (any other charge), or a cost of the eviction itself: `eviction_fee`, `attorney_fee` or `court_cost`. A charge only; a payment has none. Where every charge has a kind, a place's documents itemise what is past due by kind (Georgia's notice demands only charges dated on or before its date, and never an `eviction_fee`, `attorney_fee` or `court_cost`, which are not owed before filing); a charge without a kind is accepted, except where the place's documents itemise the ledger by kind (Georgia full-service nonpayment cases today), where every charge must have a kind at submission.

sealedEnvelope.description: Whether the notice already served was posted in a sealed envelope on the door of the premises, as the person states it. Asked for where a place's filing states it (Georgia): the filing says so, and a posted notice answered `false` there does not pass the prior-notice check.

Live cases only: landlords are real owners, so a test case never takes one. 422 `landlord_not_found` for a landlord that is not one of the organization's active landlords, and for any landlord on a test case.

For a signed-in session: `permission_denied`, the person's role in the organization lacks the permission this needs (ask an owner); `no_organization`, the person belongs to no organization yet (start one with `POST /v1/me/organizations` or accept an invitation).

409.description: The request conflicts with the current state: for a case, it is not in a state that allows this, or its details were erased (`erased`); for an API key, a limit or the key in use.

422.description: The case did not pass a check.

get.summary: The prices in force: the platform fee for each starting step and the flat attorney fees of the published states. No credential; cached for a minute

200.description: The platform fees in cents and the published states' attorney fees.

changedAt.description: When these prices were last saved; null while the built-in prices are in force.

post.summary: Send a website request: access, a partner-attorney application, or a message. No credential; browser calls are allowed from the website origin only

202.description: The request was received. A request with the `contact_url` honeypot field filled in gets the same answer and is discarded.

413.description: The request body is too large.

429.description: Too many requests from this address: at most 5 every 10 minutes. `Retry-After` gives the seconds to wait.

SessionToken.description: A session token (`ess_...`) from `POST /v1/auth/signup` or `/v1/auth/login`, valid for 30 days. On the case, webhook, API key and organization routes it acts for the organization the session is in (`POST /v1/me/organization` switches it) in the mode named by the `X-Evictions-Mode` header: `test` (the default) or `live`.

AttorneyToken.description: A user token (`eut_...`) of a verified attorney.

state.description: Position in the case lifecycle, for example `notice_review` or `filing_submitted`.

openedBy.description: Who opened the case: the person (`id`, and their current display name, `null` when they have none), `{ "kind": "api_key" }` when it was opened with an API key, or `null` when that is not known (a case from before this was recorded).

landlord.description: The owner your organization acts for on this case (one of `GET /v1/landlords`), with its current name; null when none was chosen, and always null on a test case. Set it with `landlordId` on `POST /v1/cases` or `PATCH /v1/cases/{id}` (live cases only).

court.description: The court the case goes to, in words, where the rules for its place say which, with the county: for example "Magistrate court of Henry County". `null` where no rule pack covers the place, and for an erased case.

handling.description: Who does the legal work. `attorney_direct`: a licensed attorney engaged for the case reviews it, serves the notice and files in court, and the platform records each step; it is what a live case is where the full-service path is not open for its property. `automated`: the built-in test pipeline of a test case. `agent_filed`, the full-service path, as we describe it to the owner: We act as your authorized agent. No attorney reviews the case. We are not a law firm and do not give legal advice. A live case is created with it wherever that path is open for the property; a test case when `POST /v1/cases` asks for `service: "full"`. It needs the owner's signed authorization (`/v1/cases/{id}/authorization`).

attorney.description: The attorney engaged for an attorney-direct case, once recorded. Null until then, and always null for a test case.

barNumber.description: The attorney's bar number in that state.

erased.description: Whether the details of the case were erased, which we do case by case on request. An erased case keeps its id, state, dates, deadline names and charges. In `data` the names and the address read `[erased]` (the state and county are kept) and every other fact is gone; `courtCaseNumber` is null; each document keeps its id and `contentHash`, its `filename` reads `[erased]` and downloading it answers 410 `erased`; messages read `[erased]`. Any request that would change the case answers 409 `erased`.

erasedAt.description: When the details were erased. Null for a case that was not erased.

sources.description: Where each answer came from, by field path (`property.line1`, `lease.monthlyRentCents`, `parties.0`, `ledger`): the kind of source, and for a file read the id of the case document it was read from. An answer with no entry was typed. Empty when no answer came from a source. Never holds a value. Send `sources` with `POST /v1/cases` or `PATCH /v1/cases/{id}` to set it (a patch replaces the whole map); a patch that changes an answer without sending `sources` removes that answer's entry.

documentId.description: The case document the answer was read from (`lease_file`, `ledger_file` and `messages` only).

agent.description: Present, and true, only for an agent-filed case (`handling: "agent_filed"`): we act as your authorized agent, no attorney reviews the case, and we are not a law firm and do not give legal advice. Every field below appears only with it.

authorization.description: Whether your authorization for us to act as your agent is signed, and whether the facts changed after it was signed (then nothing more is done until you sign again).

complaintSignature.description: Whether the court requires the owner to sign the complaint, and whether the current complaint is signed. While it is required and unsigned, the case waits in `filing_approved`. `sworn` (true when present): the filing is an affidavit your named person swears under oath by electronic verification in the app. `signer`: the member the case names to sign it, by user id and the name the filing prints; only that person can sign.

paymentMethodId.description: The organization's saved card (`GET /v1/payment-methods`) this case's costs are charged to, or null for the default card. Choose it with `PATCH /v1/cases/{id}`. A chosen card that is removed or declined is not charged: the default card is used instead.

tasks.description: Each outward step of the case, oldest first (as `GET /v1/cases/{id}/tasks`).

checking.description: Present while we check what the next step sends before it is sent (we check every notice, filing and summons for now): `notice` (the notice to the tenant), `filing` (the court filing) or `summons`. Nothing is sent, and nothing is charged for that step, until it is checked.

sentBack.description: Present while the case is on hold because we checked a step before sending it and sent the case back to you: nothing was sent. `note` says why; reply by email, or withdraw the case.

claim.description: What the complaint asks the court for besides possession: unpaid rent, where the court lets us claim it as your agent, up to the court's limit where it has one.

amountClaimedCents.description: US cents. Zero when no rent is claimed.

hearing.description: The hearing, once the court has set one (or moved it): where the owner attends in person (`clientAttends`), you must attend it yourself; no one from the platform appears in your place.

time.description: The court's local time, HH:MM, when known.

place.description: Where the court sits for the hearing, when known.

purpose.description: What an uploaded file (`kind: "evidence"`) is for, as given with the upload. Null for documents the platform or the attorney adds, and for files uploaded before purposes were kept.

contentType.description: Decided from the file's first bytes when it was stored, never from its name. `text/plain` only for a `correspondence` document that is plain text (the body of a forwarded email).

contentHash.description: SHA-256 of the document bytes. An attorney approval names these.

PmsConnection.description: The organization's stored connection to a property-management system. Its credentials are kept encrypted and never returned.

label.description: The name the organization gave it; the system's name by default.

lastError.description: How the last search or pull failed (`unauthorized`, `rate_limited`, `unavailable`); null when it worked.

LeaseMatch.description: A lease a search found, as the property-management system holds it. Empty strings where it has nothing to show.

name.description: The system's own name for the lease (DoorLoop).

balanceCents.description: What the system says the tenant owes.

PmsPull.description: One lease read from the property-management system as suggested answers for a new case (each `{ value, source }`, the source being the system), the lease PDF when the system holds one, and the system's balance to check the ledger rows against. Nothing of it is stored: the person checks every answer.

skippedRows.description: How many ledger rows were left out because their transaction type is not one we map. Absent when none.

IntakeFile.description: A file waiting in the organization's intake inbox for a case: a PDF, JPEG or PNG the customer already has, or the plain text of a forwarded email. It waits 30 days, then is deleted unless it was moved onto a case.

source.description: How it arrived: forwarded by email, or sent through the API (an AI agent or an integration).

contentType.description: Decided from the file's first bytes, never from its name. `text/plain` only for the text of a forwarded email, stored by us.

purposeGuess.description: What the file is probably for: as sent, or guessed from its name. Confirmed when it is moved onto a case.

note.description: The email's subject or the sender's note; null when none.

expiresAt.description: When the file is deleted if it has not been moved onto a case.

Charge.description: An amount owed to the platform for a case: the platform fee, or court or service costs passed on at cost. The attorney's legal fee is never a charge here: it is separate and paid to the attorney.

collection.description: How the charge is paid. `checkout`: on the payment page (`POST /v1/cases/{id}/charges/{chargeId}/checkout`). `automatic`: a cost of a full-service case, taken from a saved card (`/v1/payment-methods`); it is never paid by checkout.

receiptUrl.description: The payment provider's public receipt page for a paid charge, kept shortly after the payment is recorded. Null until then, when it could not be read, and for charges paid before receipt links were kept (their receipt was sent by email).

PaymentMethod.description: The default card for the automatic charges of full-service cases, in the key's mode, as the older `/v1/payment-method` routes show it: its brand and last four only. `failed`: the card was declined, and the cases waiting on a payment stay on hold until a card that works is saved.

Card.description: One of the organization's saved cards for the automatic charges of full-service cases, in the key's mode. The card number is never stored: only its brand and last four. A case is charged to the card it names (`paymentMethodId`), else to the default card. `failed`: the card was declined; it is not charged again, and cannot be made the default.

label.description: What the organization calls the card, such as "Operating account card"; null when unnamed.

isDefault.description: The card charged when a case names none. One card per mode at most.

addedBy.description: The person who added it; null for a card added with an API key, or before this was kept.

Landlord.description: An owner the organization acts for, as a property manager: a profile reused across cases, never an account. It belongs to the organization, whatever the mode, and only live cases take one: a live key and a signed-in person see it, a test key never does. An archived landlord keeps its cases and is hidden from `GET /v1/landlords` unless `includeArchived=true`. At most 1,000 per organization, archived ones included.

isEntity.description: A company, trust or other entity rather than a person.

plaintiffType.description: The legal type of the plaintiff, as the full service asks it; null when not given.

ownerOfRecord.description: The owner of record of the properties; the name unless given.

notes.description: The organization's own notes; never on a court document.

caseCount.description: How many of the organization's cases in the key's mode name this landlord.

LandlordDocument.description: A landlord's management agreement, without its contents. A PDF, JPEG or PNG, decided from the file's first bytes.

CustomerCharge.description: A charge on one of the organization's cases, as the billing page lists it: the case's id, the property's state and the case's landlord, and the charge as `GET /v1/cases/{id}/charges` shows it.

propertyState.description: Two-letter code of the property's state. Empty for a case whose details were erased.

landlord.description: The case's landlord (one of `GET /v1/landlords`, archived ones too) with its current name; null when the case has none.

ChargeTotals.description: The billing page's totals over all the organization's charges in the mode, whatever the filter, in US cents. Years are UTC calendar years. "Refunded this year" counts charges by the day they were refunded.

Note.description: A message on a case, between the customer and the platform.

Authorization.description: The authorization the owner signs for an agent-filed case: the text to sign now, the signature in force for it, and whether the case facts changed after it was signed. A change to the facts makes the signature stale until the owner signs again.

textVersion.description: The version of the text, recorded with every signature.

text.description: The text the owner signs: plain text, numbered paragraphs.

recorded.description: Set when the owner gave the authorization to our staff orally (by telephone, text message, in person or email) and our staff recorded it on the owner's instruction: how and on what day. Null for an authorization signed here.

stale.description: True when the facts changed after the signature. The case does not proceed until it is signed again.

Signature.description: A signature the owner just gave. The IP address it was given from is kept only as a hash, and is not shown.

ComplaintToSign.description: The complaint documents the owner signs where the county requires the owner to sign the complaint itself, and whether exactly this set is signed.

sworn.description: Present where the court filing is an affidavit your named person swears under oath by electronic verification in the app (Georgia: O.C.G.A. § 15-10-53(d)(4)). `affiantName` is the name the affidavit prints, which the signer types; `date` is the day it is dated if sworn now (null once sworn); `documents` are the documents exactly as they will be filed if sworn now, signed and dated (download each from `GET /v1/cases/{id}/signatures/complaint/documents/{specId}`; empty once sworn). Send their `contentHash` values as `documentHashes` when signing.

Task.description: One outward step of a full-service case (`handling: "agent_filed"`): delivering the notice, filing, ordering the summons, attending the hearing, a signature from the owner, or mail from the court.

dueAt.description: When the step must be done by, when there is a deadline.

action.description: The proposed act the answer is about.

declared.description: Whether the customer declared these facts, and not only a suggestion.

declaredAt.description: When the customer declared them last.

problem.description: Why the stored facts do not read as a complete declaration.

missing.description: The facts this act is missing, each with the question to ask. An empty list is not permission to perform the act.

sources.description: Where each declared fact came from: the source of the last write that set it, `customer` or `suggestion`. A fact that is absent was never declared by anyone.

Filing.description: A submission to the court. Attorney-only.

rejectionReasons.description: The court's reasons, when it rejected the filing.

ServiceAttempt.description: One request to serve a document on one defendant. Attorney-only.

failureReason.description: The process server's reason, when service failed.

Attention.description: Whether the case needs the attorney: it is on hold, or a job for it failed for good after its last state change.

AttorneyCase.description: The case as its assigned attorney sees it. Each read is recorded in the audit log as `tenant_data_viewed`.

events.description: The full audit trail, including internal events.
